title: JOINs with filters and grouping
explanation: Here's the cool part: once two tables are joined, it's just one big table. That means everything you've learned still works on it: WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY, COUNT, all of it. The order you write it in stays the same: SELECT, FROM, JOIN ... ON, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY, LIMIT.

example.code:
SELECT s.studio_name, MAX(g.rating) AS best_rating
FROM games AS g
INNER JOIN studios AS s
  ON g.studio_id = s.studio_id
GROUP BY s.studio_name;

lines.explain: Show each studio's name and its highest-rated game's rating.
Make one group per studio, so MAX works on each studio's games.

tasks.prompt: Show each studio's name and how many games it made (call it num_games).
tasks.answer: SELECT s.studio_name, COUNT(*) AS num_games FROM games AS g INNER JOIN studios AS s ON g.studio_id = s.studio_id GROUP BY s.studio_name;
hints: Join the tables, then GROUP BY the studio name and COUNT.
... ON g.studio_id = s.studio_id GROUP BY s.studio_name

solution_lines.explain: Show each studio and how many games it has.

tasks.prompt: Show only the studios that made more than 1 game, with their count (call it num_games).
tasks.answer: SELECT s.studio_name, COUNT(*) AS num_games FROM games AS g INNER JOIN studios AS s ON g.studio_id = s.studio_id GROUP BY s.studio_name HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
hints: Same as task 1, plus HAVING to filter the groups.

solution_lines.explain: Show each studio and its count.
Only keep studios with more than 1 game.

tasks.prompt: For each studio country, show how many games come from there (call it num_games) and the best rating (call it best_rating).
tasks.answer: SELECT s.country, COUNT(*) AS num_games, MAX(g.rating) AS best_rating FROM games AS g INNER JOIN studios AS s ON g.studio_id = s.studio_id GROUP BY s.country;
hints: Group by the country from the studios table. You can use two aggregate functions at once.
SELECT s.country, COUNT(*) AS num_games, MAX(g.rating) AS best_rating ... GROUP BY s.country

solution_lines.line: SELECT s.country, COUNT(*) AS num_games, MAX(g.rating) AS best_rating
solution_lines.explain: Show each country, how many games, and the highest rating.
Make one group per studio country.

tasks.prompt: For studios founded before 2000, show the studio name and how many games it made (call it num_games), sorted by studio name A to Z.
tasks.answer: SELECT s.studio_name, COUNT(*) AS num_games FROM games AS g INNER JOIN studios AS s ON g.studio_id = s.studio_id WHERE s.founded_year < 2000 GROUP BY s.studio_name ORDER BY s.studio_name ASC;
hints: Filter rows with WHERE before grouping, then sort at the end.
... WHERE s.founded_year < 2000 GROUP BY s.studio_name ORDER BY s.studio_name ASC

solution_lines.explain: Show each studio and its count.
Only keep games from studios founded before 2000.
Sort by studio name, A to Z.

tasks.prompt: Predict first: how many rows will this return?
tasks.code:
SELECT s.studio_name, COUNT(*)
FROM games AS g
INNER JOIN studios AS s
  ON g.studio_id = s.studio_id
WHERE g.price = 0
GROUP BY s.studio_name;
hints: First find the free games, then see which studios made them.
The free games are Fortnite, League of Legends, and Valorant. Two of them come from the same studio.

solution_lines.explain: Keep only the 3 free games: Fortnite, League of Legends, and Valorant.
Group them by studio: Epic Games made 1, and Riot Games made 2. That's 2 groups, so 2 rows.

recap: You just learned that a JOIN makes one big table, so WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, and ORDER BY all work on it just like before.
